data.heading: Christmas Light Installation in Nampa, ID
data.subheading: Cold, icy Nampa rooflines make hanging your own holiday lights risky. We design, install, take down, and store a display that looks great and keeps you off the ladder.

data.body:
Everybody loves the look of a house lit up for the holidays. Nobody loves standing on an icy ladder in December to make it happen. In Nampa, roofs get cold and slick well before the season really starts, and that is exactly when homeowners are up there trying to string lights with numb hands. It is the kind of job that ends in a fall more often than people expect.

Monarch Pro Wash is an owner-run, insured company serving Nampa and the Treasure Valley. We handle the whole holiday display for you, from design and install to takedown and storage when the season is over. With more than fifteen years of exterior work on Nampa homes, we are comfortable and careful up on a roof so you never have to be.

data.heading: Christmas Light Installation Built for Nampa Conditions
data.body:
The reason to hand this job off is right there on your roof. By the time the holidays roll around, Nampa rooflines are cold and often iced over, and a slick ladder plus a steep, frosted roof is how weekend projects turn into emergency room visits. We do this work through the season, insured and equipped for it, so the risky part is on us instead of you.

Nampa homes are all different, and so are their displays. In the Old Nampa Historic District, older homes with detailed rooflines and mature trees call for a design that fits the character of the house. Out in the newer South Nampa subdivisions like Southern Ridge, Meadowcrest, and Ederra, the newer builds have their own lines and peaks to work with. We plan the display around your specific home so it looks intentional, not thrown up.

Timing matters too. The stretch from November through January is when Nampa weather is least forgiving, and it is also the whole holiday window. We install early in the season while conditions still allow, keep an eye on the display through the holidays, and come back to take everything down and store it once the season wraps, so you are not up on an icy roof in January either.
